comparison: Both address C1 (background on limitations of existing models). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED as established knowledge; peer reviewers also accept this background claim without challenge.

Both address C2 and C33-C42 (haemGx protocol and hematopoietic generation). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with strong experimental evidence; peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, questioning whether the system captures sequential waves versus progressive maturation of a single wave, with concerns about 'spatio-temporal accuracy' claims.

Both address C43-C49 (phenotypic characterization of HSPCs). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with thorough flow cytometry and functional data; peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, noting lack of robust functional validation weakens claims about lymphoid or pre-HSC-like populations.

Both address C50-C55 (distinct hematopoietic waves). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on qPCR and EZH2 inhibition data; peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 critically noting absence of HOXA9 expression argues against AGM-type hematopoiesis.

Both address C56-C62 (scRNA-seq clustering and cell types). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with adequate quality control and analysis; peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, expressing concerns about interpretation, particularly regarding HOXA9 expression and lymphoid marker claims in Cluster 8.

Both address C63-C73 (scRNA-seq gene expression patterns). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with detailed temporal analysis; peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN with same concerns as R8/R4 pairing, questioning AGM-like characteristics and lymphoid marker interpretation.

Both address C74-C79 (projection onto published datasets). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with convergent mapping across datasets; peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, noting cells might more closely resemble YS-derived EHT rather than AGM, suggesting system recapitulates multipotent lymphoid progenitors from YS.

Both address C80-C89 (engraftment data). OpenEval marks UNCERTAIN due to low engraftment levels, small sample size, and lack of long-term engraftment; peer reviewers also mark UNCERTAIN, noting data 'not particularly convincing,' questioning 8-week termination, and stating results remain marginal without HSC-level repopulation.

Both address C91 (GSEA of patient transcriptomes). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as background; peer reviewers include this in their SUPPORTED evaluation of MNX1 overexpression effects, though note interpretability is limited by underlying haemGx characterization concerns.

Both address C92-C94 (MNX1 effects on haemGx morphology and cellularity). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with statistical significance; peer reviewers mark SUPPORTED, finding MNX1 overexpression experiments 'generally convincing' for early expansion effects.

Both address C95-C99 (MNX1 transcriptional effects). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with comprehensive RNA-seq analysis showing selective targeting of YS-like programs; peer reviewers mark SUPPORTED, acknowledging transcriptional resemblance to MNX1-r AML.

Both address C100-C101 (GSEA enrichment in MNX1-OE and patients). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with important validation of patient biology recapitulation; peer reviewers include in SUPPORTED evaluation but note interpretability limitations.

Both address C102-C105 (serial replating assays). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as classical indicator of transformation; peer reviewers mark SUPPORTED but note transformation evidence is solely in vitro without in vivo leukemia engraftment.

Both address C106-C111 (replating transcriptional signatures). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with convergent evidence of patient biology recapitulation; peer reviewers mark SUPPORTED but emphasize lack of in vivo validation limits transformation claims.

Both address C112-C113 (cytospin morphology). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with morphological progression data; peer reviewers mark SUPPORTED as part of overall MNX1 experiments but note in vivo validation gap.

Both address C5-C6 (main conclusions about MNX1 targeting YS-like progenitors). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with convergent evidence; peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, acknowledging transcriptional similarity to patients but noting lack of in vivo leukemia engraftment and need for future studies on transformation dynamics.
Both address C4 (background on infant AML). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as established knowledge; peer reviewers also mark SUPPORTED without challenge.

Both address C7-C18 (background on embryonic hematopoiesis). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as established knowledge; peer reviewers also mark SUPPORTED, accepting these background claims to establish scientific context.
Both address C19-C30 (background on pediatric leukemia and MNX1-r AML). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as established knowledge; peer reviewers also mark SUPPORTED without challenge.

Both address C31-C32 (background on gastruloid models). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as established knowledge; peer reviewers also mark SUPPORTED, with acknowledgment that gastruloids are useful for studying early embryonic development.
Both address C90 (background on MNX1-r AML characteristics). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as prior literature; peer reviewers also mark SUPPORTED without challenge.

OpenEval R19 addresses major conclusions including C2 (haemGx recapitulates hematopoiesis); peer R1 addresses C2 with protocol claims C33-C42. OpenEval finds C2 well-supported; peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN with concerns about sequential waves versus single wave maturation.
